correctness.rationale: Core matchings A of any finite simple G are in bijection with maximal matchings of G◦K1, adjoining exactly the leaf edges of unmatched core vertices. If two such matchings have the same observed trace, their symmetric difference uses unobserved core edges and splits into alternating even cycles and paths; each path's endpoints both have omitted leaf observations in the same R-component. Conversely an even cycle gives two alternating matchings with same saturation pattern, while a path between two omitted leaf endpoints gives an indistinguishable pair (parity of path edge count determines endpoint saturation, both hidden). Thus forcing iff H=(V,R) is even-cycle-free and each H-component contains at most one omitted-leaf vertex. For fixed R, maximum omitted edge count is |R|+c(H)=n+β(H), yielding φ_gm=m−max β(H). A graph without even cycles has odd simple cyclic blocks forming an odd cactus: intersecting odd cycles along more than one vertex would make an even cycle. Bipartite G has no odd cycle so b=0, and any odd cycle yields b≥1. For P_n, weighted compositions of component interval lengths give generating function (1−z)²/(1−3z+z²) with coefficient F_{2n}; C_n and K_n boundaries are handled explicitly. Independent source-definition enumeration of every labelled G on ≤4 vertices checked 11,894 observation masks against the stated structural criterion and optimum; this corroborates but does not replace the universal alternating-path proof.

value.rationale: Global forcing for maximal matchings is a classical natural edge-identification problem. The earlier literature specifically raised whether the standard corona bound is sharp for other graphs; the exact all-base criterion answers that mathematical question in structural terms, explains deviations through an odd-cactus cycle-rank invariant, and enumerates complete optimum witnesses. This is a uniform nontrivial structural result beyond recomputing known isolated values, even though b_odd is not given in closed form for arbitrary G.
